body:
Please upload an MRP to make this easier to test, fix, and confirm:
- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue, with no unnecessary files included. Be sure to not include the `.godot` folder in the archive (but keep `project.godot`).
- Having an MRP is very important for contributors to be able to reproduce the bug in the same way that you are experiencing it. When testing a potential fix for the issue, contributors will use the MRP to validate that the fix is working as intended.
- Drag and drop a ZIP archive to upload it (max 10 MB). **Do not select another field until the project is done uploading.**
- **Note for C# users:** If your issue is *not* C#-specific, please upload a minimal reproduction project written in GDScript. This will make it easier for contributors to reproduce the issue locally as not everyone has a .NET setup available.

I think I was mistaken. It appears the issue actually has to do with rendering a subtractive blended material in a SubViewport for a ViewportTexture, as I make use of those in my project.

However, it still is broken in Editor as well.

Here is an MRP to test it in v4.4.dev5.official [9e6098432] :
[SubtractBlending_4.4-dev5.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17874945/SubtractBlending_4.4-dev5.zip)

If you open it, you can see it broken in the Editor. When run, you can see that it just displays a grey box. You can adjust the MeshInstance3D's Material to Add, or Multiply and it will work fine. Subtract seems to cause issues.

Can reproduce on 4.5-master (215acd52e8), Windows 11, Nvidia GeForce RTX 4070.

For comparison, this is what it looks like with the Forward+ renderer (Mobile is similar, as well Compatibility without the SubViewport):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b720006e-45de-4ceb-8719-9f4baabe7e70)

Whereas with Compatibility, it looks like this:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b80b6c20-c2bb-4665-b18f-cd41c1f6675e)

The color in-game is `rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color` (you can see this by changing the project setting to something other than grey), despite the MRP having a WorldEnvironment with a clear color.  In the SubViewport's preview window it looks like this, which suggests that alpha is being subtracted:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/438f5fa7-665b-45e6-9139-30a40c201934)

@AThousandShips
